# On the hull-full upgrade screen show current upgrades

**Headline:** Add a permanent-only "currently owned upgrades/weapons" panel to the top-left of the hold-full choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`), derived from the run's permanent weapon and power-up levels so a temporary field pickup can never appear in it or inflate a displayed level.

## Original request (verbatim)

> When the player is offered a hull full upgrade they are given a list of three items, ones that are new are labelled, ones that are upgrades show the upgrade parameters. We also need to list (in the top left) the currently owned upgrades/weapons. This list should not include temporary, only permanent upgrades. If they show a level they should show only the permanent level not any temporary level upgrades.

> **Terminology:** the request says "hull full"; the shipped feature is the **hold-full choice** overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`, GDD §4.4.1), opened when the mineral hold fills. This brief treats "hull-full" as "hold-full", consistent with AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR and AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF.

## Problem statement

The hold-full choice now shows each offered item's name, a one-line description and (for levelled offers) a level-accurate change summary, plus a `★ New` badge for items the player does not own (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR, AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD, AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON). What the screen still hides is the **other half of the picture**: the build the player already has. A player offered "Spread Shot Lv.3" cannot see whether they own Rapid Fire Lv.4 or a Shield, so a levelled choice is made blind. The overlay is also the only moment where gameplay is paused and a permanent decision is taken, so it is the natural place to show the current permanent loadout.

## Users

- **Player (informed build choice):** "As a player, when the hold fills, I want to see everything I already own permanently — weapons and power-ups, with their permanent levels — so I can judge whether a new offer fits my build."
- **Player (no mental arithmetic):** "As a player, I don't want my displayed level to include a 10-second field pickup I happened to catch, because the permanent level is what the offer is priced against."
- **Designer/tuner:** "As a designer, I want the list derived from the same permanent-only snapshots the choice pool already uses, so the panel can never disagree with what is offered."

### Example user stories

- As a player with `Spread Shot Lv.2`, `Rapid Fire Lv.1` and `Shield Lv.3` permanently owned, I see those three listed top-left when the hold fills.
- As a player who caught a field `Spread Shot` five seconds ago (temporary stack only, no permanent grant), the panel does **not** list Spread Shot, and if I own `Rapid Fire Lv.1` the panel shows `Lv.1`, not `Lv.2`.
- As a player opening the very first hold-full choice of a run, the panel tells me plainly that I own nothing permanent yet.

## Acceptance Criteria

> The three presentation decisions were confirmed by the producer during intake (Q1 = A, Q2 = A, Q3 = A; see the Appendix).

- **AC1 — Owned permanent items are listed.** The hold-full overlay renders, in the top-left of the screen, every item the player owns **permanently** this run — permanent **weapons and power-ups** — as one row per item. The permanent `cannon` is excluded (it is the base weapon, never a permanent reward) and so is the `reset` utility.
- **AC2 — Permanent only.** Temporary (field-pickup) upgrades never appear in the panel, and a displayed level is the item's **permanent level only** (`getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()`), never `permanent + temporary`. A field-only item is absent from the panel and still offered as `★ New`.
- **AC3 — Single source of truth.** The panel's item names come from the shared choice/catalogue naming (`toChoiceOption(id).name` in `src/powerups/choice.ts`, itself backed by `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` / `WEAPON_NAMES`); no second name table or duplicated level arithmetic is introduced in the scene.
- **AC4 — Level display.** Every row always shows the item's permanent level as `Lv.N`, including `Lv.1` (e.g. `Spread Shot Lv.2`, `Shield Lv.3`, `Rapid Fire Lv.1`), matching the offer labels on the same screen so a level-1 item and a levelled item are unambiguously distinguishable.
- **AC5 — Presentation & empty state.** The panel is a **single flat list** under the heading `YOUR UPGRADES`, rendered top-left (weapons first, then power-ups, catalogue order within each kind, so the order is deterministic). When the player owns nothing permanently, the heading reads `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` rather than an empty/blank region. The panel must not collide with the centred option column (3 options, `CHOICE_FIRST_ROW_Y`…`+ pitch × 2`) at the shipped game resolution.
- **AC6 — Gym↔game parity.** Every launcher that opens the hold-full choice (`PlayScene.openMineralChoice`, `GymFormationScene.openMineralChoice`, `GymWeaponLeveling.openMineralChoice`, `GymPowerUpLeveling.openMineralChoice`) supplies the same permanent snapshots it already passes to the strategy context, so the panel behaves identically in the game and every gym; no divergent copy.
- **AC7 — Teardown & lifecycle.** The panel is destroyed with the rest of the choice UI when a selection starts the 3-2-1 countdown, and is rebuilt from current state the next time the overlay opens (no stale carry-over between hold-full events).
- **AC8 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the pure owned-loadout builder (permanent-only filtering, cannon/`reset` exclusion, deterministic ordering, `Lv.N` labels, empty case) and scene tests cover the rendered rows, the empty state, the teardown, and that a temporary-only weapon/power-up never appears and never raises a displayed level. Every test asserts a meaningful behaviour (TDD preferred).
- **AC9 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (where the overlay is described) and GDD §4.4.1 (hold-full choice presentation).
- **AC10 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** behaviour lives once — a pure builder consumed through the launcher payload, rendered by the single shared `MineralChoiceScene`; the duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs assertion must stay green.
- **Backward compatibility:** the overlay's `init` payload gains an **optional** field; isolated scene tests that launch it with `options` only must keep working (absence → panel omitted or empty state, decided by the implementation and covered by a test).
- **No live mutation:** the panel reflects the permanent snapshots captured at launch; it need not update while the overlay is open (the choice is applied after the countdown, at which point the overlay closes).
- **Do not change the offered options, their order, the change summaries, the `★ New` badge, or the 3-offer mechanism** — this item is additive presentation.
- **Keep the existing accessors intact:** `getOptionLabels()`, `getDetailLines()`, `getDescriptionLines()` assertions must not break; add a new accessor for the panel rows.
- **Bounded list:** the six-slot permanent cap (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF, `src/powerups/slots.ts`) bounds the list to ≤ 6 kinds plus any `availableWhenSlotsFull` exemptions, so no scrolling/paging design is required.
- **Run-scoped only:** no leaderboard or persistence impact.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — modal overlay: opaque backdrop, `HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP` heading at `y = 120`, one centred option block every `CHOICE_ROW_PITCH = 84` px from `CHOICE_FIRST_ROW_Y = 200` (name → description → change summary/`★ New`); `getOptionLabels()` / `getDetailLines()` / `getDescriptionLines()`; `_teardownChoiceUi()` destroys backdrop, heading, controls, detail/description lines and the keydown listener when the countdown starts.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `openMineralChoice()` — already computes `weaponLevels: player.getWeaponLevels()` and `powerUpLevels: player.getPowerUpLevels()` for the strategy context, but passes only `options`, `fireSchedule`, demo auto-select params and `onSelect` to `scene.launch('MineralChoiceScene', …)`.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — same pattern (compute the two snapshots, pass options + `fireSchedule` + `onSelect`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `openMiniBossReward()` — also launches `MineralChoiceScene`, with `buildUpgradeOptions({ weaponLevels, powerUpLevels })`; **no** owned panel supplied today (see Risks).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `ChoiceOption`, `toChoiceOption(id)` (name + description from the shared catalogues), `WEAPON_NAMES`, `buildLevelUpOption`, `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — `resolveSlotState(powerUpLevels, weaponLevels)` → `{ used, free, isFull, ownedIds }`; already filters the permanent `cannon` and derives occupancy from the two **permanent-only** snapshots.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `getWeaponLevels()` (permanent weapon grants only) and `getPowerUpLevels()` → `PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` (permanent power-up grants only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — existing owned-item row label convention `"<Name> Lvl <N>"` for the in-run HUD rows.
- GDD §4.4.1 documents the hold-full choice overlay, its option copy and the change-summary/`★ New` contract; its **Permanent pick** bullet names only `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and `GymWeaponLeveling` as launchers.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — the hold-full launcher parity guard ("every launcher passes the common overlay payload", `HOLDFULL_LAUNCHERS`) lists only `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` also launches the overlay but is **absent** from that list.
- `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` — the existing §4.4.1 docs guard (overlay option copy); `src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts` holds the same `holdFullChoiceSection()` helper pattern.

## Desired change

1. **Pure owned-loadout builder (new module, e.g. `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts`)** — `buildOwnedLoadout(powerUpLevels, weaponLevels)` returning the permanent loadout as display rows (`{ id, kind, name, level, label }`), ordered deterministically (weapons first, then power-ups, catalogue order within each kind), each labelled `"<Name> Lv.<N>"`. Filters non-drop ids (`cannon`, `reset`) via the existing `isWeaponDrop` guard and names rows through `toChoiceOption(id).name`, so naming stays single-sourced.
2. **Overlay payload** — `MineralChoiceScene.init` accepts the built rows (optional); `create()` renders them top-left as the `YOUR UPGRADES` heading plus one `Lv.N` row per item (and the `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` empty state), stored for teardown and exposed via a new test accessor (e.g. `getOwnedUpgradeLines()`); `_teardownChoiceUi()` destroys them.
3. **Launchers** — each hold-full launcher passes the rows built from the **same** `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` snapshots it already gathers for the strategy, so the panel and the offers can never disagree. `GymPowerUpLeveling` currently passes **only** `powerUpLevels` to the strategy context, so it adds a `this.player?.getWeaponLevels() ?? []` read for the panel rows (a read of the same permanent snapshot, not new state); its offer pool stays power-ups-only. See the Open Question below.
4. **Tests and documentation** — as per AC8/AC9: builder unit tests plus scene assertions for the panel rows, empty state, teardown and temporary-level exclusion; extend the **hold-full launcher parity guard** (add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` to `HOLDFULL_LAUNCHERS` and assert every launcher passes the owned rows); add launcher-level assertions that each hold-full scene forwards the rows; update GDD §4.4.1 (panel, permanent-only rule, and the launcher list that omits `GymPowerUpLeveling`) and extend the §4.4.1 docs guard in `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` so the panel copy cannot silently drift.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts` *(new)* — pure permanent-loadout builder; filters non-drop ids, names via `toChoiceOption`, formats the level label.
- `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.test.ts` *(new)* — permanent-only filtering, ordering, labels, empty case, temporary-only exclusion.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — top-left panel rendering, empty state, teardown, `getOwnedUpgradeLines()`.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — panel rows/empty state/teardown/temporary-exclusion assertions.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — pass the built rows to the overlay launch payload.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend `HOLDFULL_LAUNCHERS` with `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` and assert every launcher passes the owned-loadout rows (AC6 · gym↔game parity).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — launcher-level assertions that the overlay receives the built rows (AC6).
- `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` — extend the §4.4.1 docs guard with the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel and its permanent-only rule (AC9).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.1 — document the owned-permanents panel and its permanent-only rule; correct the launcher list in the **Permanent pick** bullet to include `GymPowerUpLeveling`.
- `README.md` — feature pointer if the overlay's capabilities are listed there.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed): built the option `changeSummary` / `★ New` detail line this panel sits beside.
- **AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD** — Upgrade and weapon descriptions (completed): added the description line and the shared catalogue copy the panel reuses.
- **AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON** — Upgrade text must reflect the actual upgrade (completed): level-accurate summaries from the permanent level.
- **AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF** — Limit the number of powerup slots (in progress): the six-slot permanent cap bounds this list to ≤ 6 kinds; `resolveSlotState` uses the same permanent-only snapshots.
- **AH-0MUX802450085VZZ / AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9 / AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Permanent vs temporary split for weapons and power-ups, and the single `PowerUpLevelStore` the panel reads.
- **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2** — Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K' (completed): the existing top-left HUD readout, hidden behind the overlay's opaque backdrop.
- **AH-0MU7JTFY1006QA8I** — HUD lives label overlapped by active power-ups list (completed): precedent for owned-item list layout care.
- GDD §4.4.1 (hold-full choice), §4.4.2 (weapon leveling), §4.4.3 (power-up leveling).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (medium):** "show current upgrades" can drift into redesigning the overlay. Mitigation: additive panel only; no change to offers, ordering, summaries or badges. Further presentation ideas become linked work items.
- **Mini-boss reward overlay (medium):** `openMiniBossReward()` reuses `MineralChoiceScene` but is not the "hull-full" screen. Default (recorded non-blocking during intake, no objection raised): the panel is supplied by the **hold-full** launchers only; adding it to the mini-boss reward is a separate, cheap follow-up if wanted.
- **Layout collision (low):** option descriptions are wide, centred text; a top-left panel must stay clear of them at the shipped resolution. Verified by a scene test asserting the panel's anchor and by manual gym check.
- **Temporary-level leakage (low):** `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` are already permanent-only, but the panel must not be tempted to read `getWeaponLevel()` / `getPowerUpLevel()` (effective levels). Guarded by a test that adds a temporary stack and asserts the displayed level is unchanged.
- **Name drift (low):** mitigated by resolving every row name through `toChoiceOption` rather than a new table.
- **Test coupling (low):** existing label/detail/description accessor assertions must keep passing — the panel is a separate set of game objects.
- **Assumption:** "hull full" = the hold-full mineral choice overlay (the only permanent-choice list), consistent with the sibling items.

## Open questions (plan review)

- **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking) — weapons panel in `GymPowerUpLeveling`.** That gym passes only `powerUpLevels` (no `weaponLevels`) to the choice strategy context, so AC1 ("every permanently-owned weapon **and** power-up") and AC6 ("the same permanent snapshots it already passes to the strategy context") disagree there. **Default recorded for implementation:** build the panel from `getWeaponLevels()` + `getPowerUpLevels()` in every launcher, including `GymPowerUpLeveling`, so the panel always states the run's true permanent loadout; that gym's offer pool stays power-ups-only and the panel does not change it. Directed to: producer (confirm or overrule the default) — it only matters if the panel must mirror a gym's disabled weapon offers instead of the run's actual loadout.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-28 — `plan` skill, auto-complete path** (pre-check: effort Small / risk Low). Six review stages run on the existing intake brief; changes kept conservative and additive: Existing state records the stale parity-guard launcher list and the existing §4.4.1 docs guard; Desired change steps 3–4 make the panel's snapshot source, the parity-guard extension and the docs-guard update explicit; Key Files gains the parity guard, the four launcher tests and the docs guard; one non-blocking Open Question records the `GymPowerUpLeveling` weapon-snapshot default. No acceptance criteria changed; no children created (one small vertical slice, no phasing needed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded during intake for AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y (operator = Producer). Research performed before asking: read `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`, `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.ts`, `src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts`, the four hold-full launchers, GDD §4.4.1–§4.4.3, and worklog items AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR, AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD, AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON, AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF. All three questions were asked together (one round, multiple-choice with a stated recommendation) and answered in one reply.

- **Q1 — Content scope: which owned items appear in the top-left list?**
  - A: Every permanently-owned power-up **and** weapon drop (the permanent cannon excluded, field-only/temporary items excluded). — **Recommended:** simplest reading of the request, and matches the shared six-slot loadout that the choice pool already prices.
  - B: Weapons only.
  - C: Power-ups only.
  - **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — every permanently-owned power-up and weapon drop; the cannon and field-only/temporary items are excluded.
  - **Research:** `Player.getWeaponLevels()` and `PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` both return permanent grants only; `resolveSlotState()` already treats power-ups and weapon drops as one shared loadout, so option A is a single flat list of at most six kinds plus slot-cap exemptions.

- **Q2 — Level format: how is the permanent level shown per row?**
  - A: Always show `Lv.N` on every row, including `Lv.1`. — **Recommended:** unambiguous and consistent with the adjacent offer labels (`"1.  Spread Shot Lv.3"`).
  - B: Show the level only when N ≥ 2 (`Spread Shot` alone at level 1).
  - C: Use the HUD's existing convention `Lvl N` (e.g. `Spread Shot Lvl 2`).
  - **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — always show `Lv.N`, including `Lv.1`.
  - **Research:** the choice option names use `Lv.N` (`buildLevelUpOption`); the in-run HUD rows use `"<Name> Lvl <N>"` (`src/ui/HUD.ts`). Both conventions already ship, so either was defensible; the request only fixes *which* level (permanent) is shown, not the formatting.

- **Q3 — Presentation: heading and layout of the panel?**
  - A: One flat list under the heading `YOUR UPGRADES`, rows like `Spread Shot Lv.2`, and `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` when nothing is permanently owned. — **Recommended:** minimum code that satisfies the request, and the names are self-explanatory.
  - B: Two grouped sections under the heading (`WEAPONS`, then `POWER-UPS`).
  - C: Flat list with slot usage in the heading (`YOUR UPGRADES 4/6`), tying the list to the six-slot cap (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF).
  - **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — one flat list under `YOUR UPGRADES`, with the `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` empty state.
  - **Research:** the panel has the full top-left quadrant free (options occupy `y ≈ 200–420`, centred), and the six-slot cap bounds the list to ≤ 6 kinds, so all three options fit without scrolling. The empty state matters because the first hold-full of a run always occurs with zero permanent upgrades.

- **Non-blocking note — mini-boss reward overlay:** flagged that `openMiniBossReward()` reuses `MineralChoiceScene`; proposed default is hold-full launchers only. No objection recorded — implemented as the default (see Risks & assumptions).

- **Assumption — "hull full":** interpreted as the **hold-full mineral choice** overlay (the only permanent-choice list), consistent with AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR and AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF. No objection raised.
- **Assumption — no live refresh:** the panel reflects the state captured when the overlay opens; the overlay closes on selection, so no mid-overlay updates are required.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** – Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed)
- **AH-0MV70Y2XY005J2HI** – Hold-full overlay: fade the thruster/engine hum out while paused (completed)
- **AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP** – F3: Weapon temporary/permanent split (completed)

# Implement: seam-aware aimed fire

Implementation slice for seam-aware aimed fire (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC2). Every archetype routed through the shared aimed-shot method — Scout, `march` and the Raider — gains shortest-wrapped-path aiming in one place.

## Goal

Compute the player delta along the shortest wrapped path before `atan2` in the shared aimed-fire seam, gated on `wrapAware`, so shots can leave one edge and arrive from the opposite edge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The wrapped-delta calculation lives once in a shared pure helper in `src/scenes/core/` (or alongside `enemyTargeting.ts`) and is imported by the aimed-fire seam — no divergent copy in any entity.
- `Scout.tryFireAimedBullet` aims along the shortest wrapped path when `wrapAware` is true, preserving every existing gate (fire interval, shot probability, advance cue/tell, `shootEnabled`, alive, spawn guard).
- Aimed-fire archetypes sharing the method (`march`, `raider`) inherit the behaviour through the same seam with no per-class copy.
- An enemy with `wrapAware: false` keeps the current direct aim — bit-identical angles for mid-arena geometry.
- Radial/spread/burst patterns are untouched (out of scope per parent constraint).
- The bullet wrap model itself is untouched; only launch direction changes.
- Build passes and the changed-scope tests (including the slice-3 tests) are green.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Scout.ts`
- `src/entities/Raider.ts`
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`

# Test: wrap-aware enemy movement

Test-first verification slice for wrap-aware movement (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC3 + AC5). Pins per-edge wrapping for wrap-aware archetypes and the unchanged bounded behaviour of the classic exclusions.

## Goal

Specify, in tests, that wrap-aware motion which would carry an enemy off-screen wraps to the opposite edge while `march` and `centipede` keep their bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests assert that crossing each of the four edges (left, right, top, bottom) relocates a wrap-aware enemy to the opposite edge, matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap model (position only — velocity preserved).
- Tests cover the shared post-motion wrap helper in isolation (pure function, no Phaser) including the exact-boundary and multi-edge-overshoot cases.
- A test asserts `march` still reverses at the arena edge and drops vertically, and that `centipede` still weaves within bounds (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts` / centipede formation unchanged).
- A regression test asserts a non-aware archetype's position is never wrapped by the shared seam even when it leaves the arena bounds.
- At least one test covers each wrap-aware movement class (dive, chase, orbit, drift, roam, hold-and-move) at the seam.
- All tests pass deterministically.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/entities/Ghost.test.ts`
- `src/entities/Asteroid.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- The tests fail against the pre-change bounded/clamped motion and pass once the shared wrap lands.

## Problem statement

The PlayScene integration test `PlayScene — Robotron homing horde (AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6) > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`) failed once during the AI_Hell full suite (heavy machine load) and passed on a fresh full-suite re-run minutes later with identical code. It is a flaky test, not a gameplay regression, and it is the last remaining kill test in this file that has not been hardened against non-deterministic scene state.

## Users

- **AI agents and producers running the full suite** — a red full-suite gate blocks `dev` pushes and triggers `test-failure` triage items and retries.
- **Developers of the Robotron horde (and shared kill seam)** — they need the horde kill/accounting contract to stay proven while the test stays stable.

Example user stories:

- *As an agent whose `implement.py finish` gate runs the full suite, I want the Robotron horde kill test to pass deterministically so that an unrelated docs-only change is never blocked by it.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the wave-accounting contract (a horde kill counted exactly once) still asserted, so the fix does not hide a real regression.*

## Existing state (evidence)

Failure from the `implement.py finish` gate for AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H (docs-only change, cannot affect kill behaviour):

```
FAIL |integration| src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once
AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6168:26
    6166|     scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
    6167|     scene.tick(0.001);
    6168|     expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
```

Same run also printed repeated `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` on stderr (unrelated noise; no test failed on it).

The current test body (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6174-6184`) is:

```ts
const victim = liveGrunts(scene)[0];
scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
scene.tick(0.001);
expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
expect(wm.enemiesAlive).toBe(total - 1);
```

Two facts narrow the cause:

1. **The test is non-deterministic per run, independent of load.** `bootWithHordeWave()` never injects an RNG or run seed, so `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` draws a fresh `randomSeed()` (`Math.random()`, `src/core/rng.ts`) each run and the horde plan (`computeHordeSpawns`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts`) places the 16 grunts at RNG-jittered points along the four arena edges. The passing re-run therefore re-drew a different layout; "passed on re-run" is *not* evidence that load is the variable.
2. **The identical scenario has already been fixed one describe-block earlier.** `killing a pursuer advances wave accounting exactly once` (Pac-Man pursuer) had the same single-`tick(0.001)` shape and the same flake, and was fixed by wrapping the kill in the existing module-level `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` helper (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:397-410`, documented as AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK): it stubs `getEnemyEntities()` to the victim only and disables auto-fire for the duration, so "auto-fire or an overlapping pursuer cannot add a second kill and double-decrement the wave accounting". The Robotron horde kill test is the *unhardened sibling* of that test — it predates/omits the isolation.

The description's original hypothesis ("the physics/collision step for that tick may not process the new projectile before the assertion") is **not** supported: `scene.tick(dt)` is a synchronous call that runs the full player/auto-fire/bullet/collision/accounting pass in one go (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1265+`), so a longer tick cannot make a pass "complete"; what changes with a longer tick is *how much extra state* (auto-fire bullets, homing movement, wave timer) participates in that pass.

## Diagnosis to confirm during implementation

Confirm the exact mechanism before changing the assertion. Candidate mechanisms, in order of likelihood:

1. **Auto-fire / other-bullet interference** — the scene's auto-fire is live in this scenario, so a shot fired in the same tick can hit a grunt (or a different, overlapping grunt) and shift which entity the spawned bullet resolves against. The pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) fixed exactly this with `isolateEnemyForKill`.
2. **Overlapping horde grunts** — grunts in one spawn group share an edge and can be placed close enough that a bullet placed on the victim is also within an earlier-iterated grunt's hit radius.
3. **Wave-phase/`paused` gating** — a wave-timeout transition switches `tick()` to the carried-survivor-only collision pass (`_handleCarriedSurvivorCollisions`), and a paused scene makes `tick()` a no-op; either would leave the victim alive. Check `scene.isTransitioning()` / `paused` under the failing seed.
4. **Wall-clock frames before the loop is stopped** — `bootScene()` resumes the live RAF loop, and `advanceGame()` stops it only after a microtask yield, so real frames with real deltas run before the deterministic stepping begins (load-dependent state drift). Relevant if the failure reproduces without seed isolation.

Reproduce deterministically (seed sweep): inject a fixed seed via `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(<seed>))` before `scene.restart()` and sweep seeds until the failure reproduces, then fix and verify that seed. Prefer the narrowest fix that removes the interference.

Steps to reproduce (seed sweep):

1. In `bootWithHordeWave()`, add `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(seed))` before `scene.scene.restart()` (import `createSeededRng` from `../core/rng`).
2. Loop seeds (e.g. `0..999`) in a temporary harness or repeated test-skill runs until `victim.alive` is `true` after the kill step; note the seed.
3. Record the seed and the observed mechanism on this work item, then apply the fix and re-verify that seed plus a broader sweep.

## Desired change

Make the horde kill test deterministic **without weakening what it proves**:

- Isolate the kill exactly as the pursuer test does — reuse `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` (`auto-fire` off, only the victim visible to the collision pass) — and/or pin the scene RNG to a fixed seed so the horde layout is reproducible.
- Keep the single-tick kill if it is deterministic after isolation; otherwise use a small bounded "tick until the victim dies" loop (guard counter, e.g. ≤ 20 frames of `0.016`) and assert the *outcome*.
- Still assert that the victim dies **and** that wave accounting drops by exactly one — and, to prove "exactly once", assert the accounting is unchanged after further ticks (no double decrement).

## Acceptance criteria

- The flaky failure is reproduced deterministically first (fixed seed and/or a temporary repeat-run harness), and the observed mechanism is recorded as a comment on this work item with the failing seed (or an explicit statement that no seed reproduces it, with the evidence gathered).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` passes on repeated runs: at least 20 consecutive runs of `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` via the test skill, and at least one run with an additional concurrent load-generating job active, all green.
- The test still proves the contract: the victim grunt is dead after the kill step, and `wm.enemiesAlive` is exactly `total - 1` (and stays `total - 1` after further ticks — a kill is never counted twice). The "exactly once" proof is not weakened to "at most once".
- The fix is confined to test code (plus test comments); no gameplay behaviour, RNG semantics, or `isSpawning`/collision logic changes. If investigation shows a genuine gameplay defect is being masked, stop and record it as a new work item (`discovered-from:AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU`) rather than loosening the test.
- If the fix pattern is reusable (e.g. other horde/pursuer kill tests), note it in the test comment referencing AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU and AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK so the next reader sees why the isolation is required.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-execution policy:** every agent-initiated test run goes through the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`) — no ad-hoc `vitest`/`npm test`. Repeated-run verification is therefore a test-skill invocation with a narrow scope (changed-scope gate) plus the full-suite gate at push.
- **No assertion weakening:** a longer tick alone is acceptable only if it is deterministic after isolation; it must not become a "sleep until it works" loop with an unbounded guard.
- **No production-code behaviour change:** the horde kill path (`_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`, `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`) is shared with every gym (`src/scenes/core/`), so a behavioural change would require gym-parity work — out of scope unless a real defect is found.
- Prefer reusing existing helpers (`isolateEnemyForKill`, `finishSpawnSequence`) over introducing a new pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — horde kill test at ~6174; `bootWithHordeWave`/`releaseHorde` helpers at ~6089-6124; existing `isolateEnemyForKill` helper at ~397-410 to reuse.
- `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` — RNG-driven spawn placement (`computeHordeSpawns`) explaining per-run layout variance.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `planHordeSpawns` / `_releaseDueHordeSpawns` (~2164-2245), `tick` collision/phase ordering (~1265-1390), `_initRunSeed` (~4849-4863).
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `randomSeed()` / `createSeededRng()` (`Math.random`-seeded runs by default).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — `bootScene`/`advanceGame` deterministic harness (frame-loop stop/resume behaviour).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies` (~1189) and `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` (~384) — read-only context for the interference analysis.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** no gameplay defect is being masked. If the isolated test still fails for a fixed seed, the flake may reflect a real horde/accounting bug — escalate as a new (child) work item instead of widening the tick.
- **Risk:** adding `scene.setRng(...)` in this describe block changes the RNG stream for the other four horde tests in the same block; keep the seed pinned in a `beforeEach`-style helper or per-test so assertions like "spawns the configured horde" stay valid.
- **Risk:** a bounded tick loop can hide a regression that makes kills take longer; keep the bound small (≈ 0.32 s simulated) and assert exactly-once accounting afterwards.
- **Risk (scope creep):** other single-tick kill tests in the same file (asteroids, boss phases) use `tick(0.016)` and have not flaked; do not refactor them wholesale — record as separate work if desired.
- **Risk:** flake attribution — a green re-run under load is weak evidence; the fix must be justified by a *reproduced deterministic* failure, not by "it passed 20 times".
- **Risk:** `isolateEnemyForKill` stubs `getEnemyEntities` and `autoFireEnabled` on the instance and must be restored in a `finally` block (as the pursuer test does); a leaked stub would silently affect later tests in the same file.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK** (completed) — `[test-failure] PlayScene — flaky wave-accounting kill tests (Harvester + Pac-Man pursuer)`; introduced `isolateEnemyForKill` for exactly this interference class. Direct precedent.
- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** (completed) — `Flaky tests: PlayScene and GymFormationScene fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load`; load-sensitivity remediation (deterministic boot/frames).
- **AH-0MV5JRAH90034PKR** (completed) — `Flaky Centipede chain bounds assertion under full-suite load`; fixed "advanced 20 s in one tick" by stepping in 0.05 s increments — precedent for tick-size fixes in this file.
- **AH-0MVFPMT4P005UHZL** — removed the last wall-clock waits from the suites (`advanceGame` / `stepGameUntil`); the deterministic harness this test relies on.
- **AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6** — the Robotron homing horde feature these tests cover.
- **AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H** (completed) — docs-only change whose gate surfaced this flake (`discovered-from`).
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — repo guard documenting the flake history and the supported deterministic replacements.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent consideration):** "Is the failure load-induced (wall-clock frame drift) or seed-induced (random horde layout)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence, no producer input needed):** seed-induced is demonstrable from the code — `bootWithHordeWave` injects no RNG, so `_initRunSeed()` draws `randomSeed()` per run and `computeHordeSpawns` places grunts at RNG-jittered edge positions. The pass-on-re-run therefore used a different layout. Load may additionally drift scene state via live RAF frames before `advanceGame` stops the loop, but that is not required to explain the flake. Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4849-4863`, `src/core/rng.ts:49`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` (`computeHordeSpawns`).
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Does the description's proposed fix (`scene.tick(0.05)` / tick-until-dead) actually address the mechanism?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence):** only partially. `scene.tick(dt)` is synchronous, so "the collision step did not process the projectile" cannot happen; the pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) shows the real interference was auto-fire / overlapping entities, fixed by `isolateEnemyForKill`. The brief therefore requires isolation (plus a fixed seed) as the primary fix, with a bounded tick loop only as a secondary robustness measure.
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Should the fix change gameplay code (e.g. horde collision ordering)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo constraints):** no. Any gameplay change is shared with every gym and would require gym-parity work; a genuine defect would be filed as a new work item instead. Assumption recorded in *Risks & assumptions*.
- **Producer input:** none required — the item's goal and acceptance criteria are unambiguous and the remaining decisions are resolved by repo evidence and precedent. Recorded here for auditability; no open questions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUJRVYWG006NJUU** – Shared multi-hit kill finalisation (completed) — the shared kill seam this test's bullet path runs through.
- **AH-0MUIGTRFY002JDDS** – Shared mineral kill-drop helper + PlayScene/BaseEnemy refactor (completed) — touches the same enemy-kill finalisation path.

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — gym↔game parity convention (§5.1), relevant to the "no behaviour change" constraint.
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — documents this flake family and the supported deterministic replacements.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `isolateEnemyForKill` helper (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) reused by the fix.

---

## Plan (produced by /skill:plan on 2026-10-28)

Decomposition into 5 children in test-first dependency order (statuses shown at plan time; blocked children released for scheduling):

1. **Reproduce horde kill flake via seed sweep** (AH-0MVRLGUTZ007V3E5, task, high) — seed-injecting `bootWithHordeWave(seed?)` via `setRunSeed`, sweep seeds 0..999 until the un-hardened kill leaves the victim alive, record failing seed + mechanism comment; or record no-reproduction evidence. Satisfies AC1.
2. **Harden horde kill test with isolation** (AH-0MVRLGZPG0036ZTV, task, high) — `isolateEnemyForKill` with `finally` restore + fixed run seed; asserts victim dead, `enemiesAlive === total - 1` and stays so after further ticks (exactly once). Test comment references AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU + AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK. Satisfies AC3-AC5.
3. **Multi-seed horde kill regression guard** (AH-0MVRLH07H001KW8S, task, medium) — committed parametrised `it.each(≥50 seeds)` proving the exactly-once contract is layout-independent. Satisfies AC3 (durable).
4. **Document the horde kill isolation pattern** (AH-0MVRLH0P6004TNSZ, docs, medium) — test-file comment + flake-history docs (`src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts`, README/docs grep). Satisfies AC6.
5. **Verify hardened horde test under load** (AH-0MVRLH178001JITL, task, high) — ≥20 consecutive test-skill runs, one under concurrent load, failing-seed regression, full-suite green; evidence comment. Satisfies AC2, AC7.

Dependency edges: 2→1, 3→2, 4→2, 5→(3,4).

**Planning-time mechanism insight (candidate strongest):** `tick()` (src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1291-1341) switches to the carried-survivor-only collision pass when `transitionTimer > 0` (wave-timeout transition) — that pass never resolves a player bullet against horde grunts, leaving `victim.alive === true` and the accounting untouched for that tick. Whether the wave-timeout lands inside `releaseHorde`'s `tick(20)` vs the 0.001 s kill tick is seed-dependent because `HORDE_SPAWN_TIME_JITTER_SECONDS = 0.25` jitters spawn-group times. Confirmation/rejection is part of the reproduce step (checked via `scene.isTransitioning()` under the failing seed).

**Duplicate handling (plan session):** AH-0MVOKZ2WK006GLFF (open, idea stage, unassigned) described the same flake with ACs fully subsumed by this item's AC1-AC3 — closed as a duplicate during planning (comment + close recorded).

**Effort/risk:** parent estimate Small/Medium (effort_and_risk_skill, 2026-10-25) retained; per-child effort/risk set manually from it (S/Medium, S/Medium, S/Low, XS/Low, S/Medium) — re-running the skill per child was skipped to avoid duplicate report comments (idempotence).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers (plan session 2026-10-28)

- **Q (Map, planning):** "Which seed-injection seam should the reproduce harness use — `setRng(createSeededRng(seed))` (as the brief suggests) or `setRunSeed(seed)`?"
  - **Answer (Map, resolved from repo evidence):** `setRunSeed(seed)` is the canonical seam — `_initRunSeed` (src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4903) reads the injected seed at the next `create()` and drives every gameplay draw, while `setRng` leaves the injected stream untouched and is documented for scripted-RNG tests. The plan therefore pins via `setRunSeed` before `scene.restart()`, with `setRng` as a fallback only if `setRunSeed` is shown not to drive the horde layout. (Child F1 AC1.)
- **Q (Map, planning):** "Is the wave-timeout transition branch a plausible mechanism for the flake, and should it be checked during reproduction?"
  - **Answer (Map, resolved from repo evidence):** yes — `tick()` gates the full collision pass behind `transitionTimer === 0`; a wave-timeout with grunts still alive switches to `_handleCarriedSurvivorCollisions`, which cannot kill a horde grunt. Spawn-time jitter makes the transition landing seed-dependent. Recorded as the planning-time mechanism insight above; F1 AC3 requires checking `scene.isTransitioning()`/`paused` under the failing seed.
- **Q (Map, planning):** "The idle open item AH-0MVOKZ2WK006GLFF covers the same flake — duplicate?"
  - **Answer (Map, resolved by AC comparison):** full duplicate — its ACs (rerun 5x, make assertion load-robust or document, declare verdict) are subsumed by this item's AC1-AC3; no work had started. Closed during planning. No producer input required (per intake Appendix).
- **OPEN QUESTION:** none — every remaining decision (isolation, seed pinning, bounded-loop guard, docs scope) is constrained by the parent ACs or resolved from repo evidence; the parent Appendix already records "no producer input required".

# We need an outer loop (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC)

## Objective

**User story (producer).** As the producer, I want the region/home-world proposal
plus **two genuinely different** outer-loop candidates, each written up as a
decision-ready outline on the same footing, so that I can choose one and have it
written into the Game Design Document (GDD) with confidence.

**User story (player).** As a player, I want something to carry forward between
runs — a long-term goal and a sense that my play changes the world — so that
losing a run does not mean losing all progress, and so that beating the final
boss is a milestone on the way to winning rather than the end of everything.

## Users

- **Producer / designer (primary).** Chooses one of three outlined loops and owns
  the GDD write-up; needs comparable, honest outlines and a defensible ranking.
- **Player (arcade / bullet-hell fan).** Needs a reason to return after a lost
  run and a goal beyond a high score; wants progress that survives failure.
- **Developer / agent implementing the loop later.** Needs each outline to name
  the systems, seams and gym coverage so the chosen loop can be planned without
  re-deriving the design.

## Problem statement

The game has a strong **inner loop** (flying, dodging formations, destroying
enemies) and a functioning **middle loop** (per-run ship upgrading through
minerals → hold-full power-up choices → levelled weapons), but **no outer loop**:
nothing persists between runs except a leaderboard score, player settings and a
single run checkpoint. A death ends the run outright (GDD §4.6: "There is no
continue mechanic. Game over is final"), so long-term engagement rests entirely
on score chasing. The fiction ("pilot a resistance ship through a digital
underworld ruled by rogue AI") implies a war to be won, but the game currently
has no structure that represents winning it.

The producer has proposed one candidate outer loop (contested regions with a
home world to find and defend) and asked for **two other candidates** to be
brainstormed and outlined, after which the producer chooses one for the GDD.

## Deliverable

A single design-exploration document — `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — built
to the same standard as the existing research catalogues
(`docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`):
selected candidates written up per-concept, a "considered but not selected"
section, and a selection recommendation. It is a **design document only**: no
gameplay code, no persistence schema changes and no new scenes are implemented
in this item.

The producer's choice is then written into the GDD as a follow-on work item; this
item ends at the candidate document, the comparison and the recommendation.

## Loop tiers used by the document

| Tier | Timescale | Definition in this game | Exists today? |
|------|-----------|-------------------------|---------------|
| **Inner** | Seconds | Flying, dodging, destroying enemies and formations within a wave | Yes (GDD §2.3–2.6) |
| **Middle** | Minutes (a run) | Ship upgrading: minerals → hold-full power-up/weapon choices, levelled effects, extra lives | Yes (GDD §4.4, §4.6) |
| **Outer** | Hours (a campaign / a season) | What the player carries **between** runs and what they are ultimately trying to achieve | **No** |

## Candidate A — Contested Regions / Home World (producer's proposal)

Recorded as proposed, not redesigned. Its outline must preserve every named
mechanic:

- Space is divided into **regions**; each region has an **AI aggression level**.
- The ship can **warp a limited distance** to adjacent regions.
- The goal is to find a region with **zero aggression** containing a **planet
  that can become home to the humans**.
- Having found it, the player must **defend all adjacent regions** against
  attack by aggressive AI.
- The player may leave their **fully upgraded ship** in a region with an **AI
  automated pilot** that defends that region.
- The player then returns home and **collects another ship with no upgrades**,
  and must go out again to make it strong enough to be left guarding another
  region.
- **Factional AI warfare** changes region strength over time: warring AI
  factions fight over a region and the winner leaves a stronger force there.
- **Win condition:** all regions have successfully defended against a massive AI
  onslaught, at which point the home world is safe and the game is won.

The outline must state its **minimal first slice** (the smallest version that
proves the loop is fun), because the full proposal is the largest of the three.

## Candidate B — Salvage Fleet (proposed direction, resource-persistent meta)

A **roguelite meta-progression** outer loop that leaves the map alone and
persists **player power** instead.

- Between runs the player spends **banked salvage** (minerals and mini-boss AI
  cores extracted at the existing checkpoint moments) in a persistent **hangar**
  to unlock hulls, starting weapons and permanent modifiers.
- Each run is a **deployment** flown in one chosen hull; losing the run forfeits
  that run's unbanked salvage but never the hangar.
- The outer goal is to assemble a fleet strong enough for a final assault run at
  maximum threat.
- Progression axis: **build/economy** (what the player owns), not territory.

## Candidate C — Signal Decode (proposed direction, knowledge-persistent meta)

A **campaign-mutating** outer loop where the thing that persists is
**information**.

- Mini-bosses and the boss drop **data fragments** that assemble a persistent
  codex revealing the origin of the AI and the "hellscape" it generates.
- Codex knowledge **mutates and unlocks the campaign** (new enemy behaviours,
  hellscape modifiers, shortcuts), and the final confrontation only becomes
  winnable once the core's rules have been decoded — the boss's phases are the
  codex's payoff.
- Progression axis: **knowledge and campaign variation**, not territory or
  currency.

## Required outline structure (every candidate)

1. **Fantasy / pitch** — one paragraph, in the game's fiction.
2. **Loop structure** — moment-to-moment → run → meta, with an explicit
   statement of *what carries between runs*.
3. **States** — win, lose, partial progress and what a bad run still advances.
4. **New systems** required (named, with rough size).
5. **Reuse of existing systems** — checkpoint (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`),
   minerals/power-up levels, `Leaderboard`, difficulty curves
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`), mini-boss rewards, bot/attract mode.
6. **Persistence and save model** — a sketch `localStorage` payload under
   §6.6 rules (defensive parse, no backend) with migration note.
7. **Session shape** — target run length and hours-to-win.
8. **UI / scene surface** — which new screens or menu entries are needed.
9. **Gym testability and the bot** — how its gameplay additions can be exercised
   in a gym (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity rule) and how attract mode can complete
   or avoid stalling on the outer loop.
10. **Pillar impact** — which current GDD pillars it changes (e.g. "no continue,
    game over is final", the single final boss), stated explicitly.
11. **Effort and risk** — sized honestly, with the failure modes that would make
    the loop unfun.
12. **Minimal first slice** — the smallest shippable version.

A **comparison table** then ranks all candidates on: fit with the existing
pilots-in-a-digital-hell fiction, reuse of shipped systems, new-system cost,
persistence complexity, session length fit, legibility of progress to the player,
gym/bot testability, and risk of trivialising or gutting the shipped campaign —
followed by an explicit **recommendation with rationale** and why the others rank
lower. A "Considered but not selected" section records further ideas (e.g. an
arcade-style tiered mutator ladder, a pure daily-seed challenge ladder) with a
one-line deferral reason each.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Deliverable exists and frames the problem.** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
   exists, opens with the inner/middle/outer tier definitions above and the
   comparison criteria, and states that it is design-only.
2. **Candidate A is complete and faithful.** Candidate A is written up with all
   twelve required sections and preserves every mechanic listed in *Candidate A*
   above (regions, limited warp, per-region aggression, zero-aggression home
   region with a habitable planet, defence of adjacent regions, autonomous-pilot
   ship hand-off, unupgraded replacement ship, faction warfare, all-regions-held
   win). No proposed mechanic is silently dropped, altered or merged.
3. **Two additional candidates, materially distinct.** Candidates B and C each
   carry all twelve required sections and each names *what persists between
   runs* differently from Candidate A and from each other; each is justified
   against at least one named design pillar or fiction element.
4. **Decision-ready comparison.** The document contains a comparison table across
   the agreed criteria, an explicit recommendation with rationale, and a ranked
   justification for why the two non-recommended candidates rank lower.
5. **Alternatives recorded.** A "Considered but not selected" section lists at
   least two further outer-loop ideas with a one-line deferral reason each.
6. **Docs guard test.** A vitest docs-guard test (convention:
   `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`) asserts the document exists,
   contains the tier definitions, the comparison table and, for each of the three
   candidates, the twelve required section headings — so the deliverable cannot
   silently regress. It passes in the changed-scope test gate.
7. **Cross-linked, not orphaned.** The new document is cross-linked from the GDD
   future-scope section (§8) and from where the other design catalogues are
   referenced in `README.md`; every added link resolves to a file or anchor that
   exists.
8. **Producer decision is staged, not pre-empted.** The document ends with a
   "Producer decision record" section (candidate | decision | date | notes) left
   pending, plus a note that the chosen loop's GDD write-up is a follow-on work
   item. No GDD gameplay text for the chosen loop is written in this item.
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `README.md`, and the GDD cross-links.
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Design only.** No gameplay, persistence-schema or scene implementation in
  this item; each candidate is marked "design only, not scheduled".
- **No backend.** All persistence must fit the existing `localStorage` model
  (GDD §6.6) with defensive parsing, as the leaderboard and checkpoint do.
- **Engine policy.** Candidates must not require a new engine or editor-driven
  content (GDD §6.1: code-first, Phaser).
- **Pillars are explicit, not accidental.** A candidate may propose changing an
  existing pillar (e.g. "no continue", the single final boss) but must say so in
  its *Pillar impact* section with a rationale and a cost.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Any gameplay element a candidate proposes must be
  exercisable in a gym scene, and the outline must say how (AGENTS.md parity
  rule, `src/scenes/gym/`, `GymFormationScene`).
- **Attract mode must not stall.** The demo bot must be able to traverse or skip
  any new outer-loop UI (§2.1 attract/demo mode).

# Unit tests: unmistakable enemy emergence + wormhole ring

Test-first contract for the per-entity and wormhole parts of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU
(approach C: no screen-space effects on the emergence path).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the unmistakable emergence treatment and the wormhole
ring/shockwave pinned by tests before implementation, so the per-entity
lifecycle (create -> shimmer -> release) and the ring lifecycle cannot regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Per-enemy outline/silhouette.** `updateEnemyShimmer` creates exactly one
  outline/silhouette layer per emerging entity on its first shimmering frame,
  pulses it during the growth window, and destroys it when growth ends.
- **Widened flicker + burst.** The alpha flicker range and the leading-edge
  ripple burst magnitudes are driven verbatim from exported tunables; the burst
  decays to zero within its documented window.
- **No residual state.** After growth ends the entity's alpha, scale and blend
  mode are restored to their pre-shimmer values, the outline is gone, and the
  per-entity shimmer clock is dropped; an entity that never shimmered is
  untouched.
- **No compounding.** Running the helper twice per frame (or with variable `dt`)
  leaves the growth scale correct (absolute-value write, no drift).
- **Wormhole ring + shockwave.** `spawnWormholeOpen` creates one ring (and one
  open shockwave pulse) per wormhole, registers them in the caller's
  `wormholeEffects` registry, and `spawnWormholeClose` stops their tweens and
  destroys them exactly once (a second close or a `SHUTDOWN` does not
  double-remove).
- **Headless no-op.** All helpers construct/update with a stubbed scene (no
  `add`/`tweens`) without throwing.
- **Test style.** Deterministic scene-tick steps (`scene.tick(dt)`), no sleeps.
- Exact teardown: the falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera filter, restoring the camera filter list with no residual state or duplicate layer. (verified by this item's tests)
- Per-enemy emergence is unmistakable per entity: outline silhouette, stronger ripple burst, widened alpha flicker, fully restored when growth ends, no screen-wide overlay. (verified by this item's tests)
- Wormhole read: a brighter larger pulsing ring plus a one-shot open shockwave, tracked in wormholeEffects and fully cleared when the wormhole closes. (verified by this item's tests)

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` — extend.

# Intake Brief — Mini Boss explosions

**Work item:** AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z (feature, high)
**Headline:** On mini-boss defeat, explode every remaining wave-gating enemy
(escorts plus the mini-boss's live minions) in a staggered sweep, add
`max(0, 30 − n)` extra explosions scattered at random across the scene plus 10
around the mini-boss's death point, and hold the mini-boss reward overlay until
every explosion animation has finished.

**Source request (verbatim):** "When the mini-boss it defeated all remaining
enemies should explode, add an additional 30 - # of enemies explosions
scattered randomly across the scene and 10 around the mini-boss. Do not show
the reward screen until all explosions have completed their animation."

## Problem statement

Defeating a mini-boss currently destroys only the mini-boss body (with its own
boss-scale explosion): surviving escorts and summoned minions stay on the field,
no celebration scatter fires, and the reward overlay opens on the same frame as
the kill — mid-explosion — so the defeat reads as abrupt rather than
celebratory. The operator wants a cascading explosion sweep on the defeat frame,
a short celebratory scatter, and the reward screen held back until the last
burst has finished animating.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, when I defeat the mini-boss I want every remaining
  enemy to blow up and an extra barrage of explosions across the screen, so the
  kill feels like a clear victory moment."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want the reward screen to appear only after the
  explosion display has finished, so I don't miss the celebration."
- **Developer/tester (gym)** — "As a tester I want the mini-boss gym's EXPLODE
  button to show the same sweep, so what I verify in the gym is what ships."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Remaining wave-gating enemies explode.** On the mini-boss's lethal
  hit, every live wave-gating enemy is destroyed in a staggered explosion sweep
  that begins on the defeat frame. Scope is **escort ships plus the mini-boss's
  live summoned minions**; non-blocking hazards (`asteroid`, `lane-traffic`, per
  `isNonBlockingHazard`) are **not** swept and remain on the field.
- **AC2 — Extra scattered explosions.** The sweep adds `max(0, 30 − n)` extra
  particle explosions, where `n` is the number of wave-gating enemies swept
  (escorts + minions), placed at positions sampled uniformly at random across
  the playfield, plus exactly **10** explosions clustered around the mini-boss's
  death position captured at destruction. Edge cases are explicit: `n = 0` → 30
  extras; `n = 30` → 0 extras; `n > 30` → 0 extras (never negative, never an
  exception). Total scattered bursts therefore never exceed 30.
- **AC3 — Reward screen waits for the explosions.** The mini-boss reward overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`, opened by `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`) opens only
  after the last explosion burst in the sweep has completed its animation. The
  `miniBossRewardOpen` latch still opens exactly one overlay per defeat, and the
  demo auto-select contract (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F) still applies after the delay
  (attract mode never stalls).
- **AC4 — Cosmetic-only destruction.** Swept enemies are removed from play but
  award **no score**, drop **no minerals / power-ups / Extra Life**, and emit
  **no kill telemetry**. Wave/level accounting still clears exactly once,
  **after** the sweep: the level advance never fires mid-display and never fires
  twice.
- **AC5 — Game↔gym parity.** `GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE path runs the **same**
  shared sweep helper as `PlayScene` (one implementation consumed by both); the
  repo duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the
  gym-parity docs assertion pass.
- **AC6 — Determinism and meaningful tests.** All random placement/jitter uses
  the run-seeded RNG (no `Math.random()` in the sweep), so a seed replays the
  same display; unit tests cover the count formula at the edges (`n = 0, 1, 29,
  30, 40`), the minion/hazard scope split, and the sweep-completion → overlay
  ordering (overlay does not open before the last burst finishes).
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries**
  (notably GDD §3.3/§4.4.4 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Shared-code parity:** the sweep lives once in a new shared module under
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss` — no
  divergent copy (AGENTS.md "Game Architecture Conventions").
- **Reuse the existing VFX:** explosions go through
  `spawnExplosionParticles` (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) — same particle
  system, ~400 ms burst lifespan, shared per-kind VFX registry
  (`getExplosionVfxCounts`). No new particle system.
- **No reward of any kind** for swept kills (operator answer Q2 = B + C): this
  is celebration VFX only, so the mini-boss reward remains the single reward
  for the encounter.
- **Ordering:** the reward overlay's `setPaused(true)` would freeze the tween
  animations, so the sweep must be allowed to run and complete before the
  overlay pauses the scene.
- **Minion capture order:** mini-boss minions are owned by the `MiniBoss` entity
  and are currently torn down by `MiniBoss.destroy()` → `_clearMinions()`
  (plain `destroy(true)`, no explosion). The sweep must capture the live minions
  (e.g. `miniBoss.getMinions()`) **before** `miniBoss.destroy()`, otherwise they
  cannot be exploded or counted in `n`.
- **Demo mode** must remain non-blocking: the delayed overlay keeps the existing
  auto-select behaviour.
- **Determinism:** seeded RNG for placement/jitter, per the repo VFX contract.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` (~L2920): on the lethal hit captures a
  `MiniBossDefeatContext`, calls `miniBoss.destroy()` (which also clears
  minions), fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` (checkpoint + reward), then replays
  one destruction through the wave state machine with a stale-count
  reconciliation guard.
- `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` calls `openMiniBossReward` **synchronously** → the
  overlay launches and `setPaused(true)` runs on the defeat frame.
- Remaining escorts/survivors are not destroyed; minions are silently torn down
  with the boss body. Hazards (`isNonBlockingHazard`) are never wave-accounted.
- `MiniBoss extends Boss`; its own death already plays a boss-scale explosion.
  `BaseEnemy.destroySelf(scale?)` / `playExplosion(scale)` is the shared
  per-enemy explosion seam, and `destroySelf()` marks the entity dead without
  awarding anything — so a cosmetic sweep can reuse it directly.
- `GymMiniBoss` destroys via EXPLODE → `MiniBoss.takeDamage()` →
  `destroySelf()`; it has no reward overlay, so the gym shows the sweep only.
- Kill accounting lives in `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` (score → drops → wave
  advance); the sweep must **not** call that path (AC4).

## Desired change

Introduce a shared `miniBossDeathSweep` helper (pure planner + thin Phaser
executor) that:

1. collects the sweep targets — live wave-gating enemies (excluding
   `isNonBlockingHazard`) plus the mini-boss's live minions captured before the
   entity is destroyed;
2. staggers their `destroySelf()` explosions over a short window so the sweep
   reads as a cascade (a modest burst scale — enemy-scale, not boss-scale);
3. spawns the `max(0, 30 − n)` random scattered extras plus 10 bursts anchored
   at the mini-boss death position, all drawn through
   `spawnExplosionParticles` with the run-seeded RNG;
4. reports completion (last burst finished) so `PlayScene` then opens the
   mini-boss reward overlay; wave accounting advances once, after the sweep.

`GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE button calls the same helper (tests observe the burst
counts and completion).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — **new** shared sweep planner
  (count/placement maths) + Phaser executor + completion callback, with tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageMiniBoss` (capture minions before
  `destroy()`), `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` / `openMiniBossReward` (defer the
  overlay until sweep completion), single deferred wave advance.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — EXPLODE path consumes the shared sweep.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — reuse `spawnExplosionParticles` /
  `getExplosionVfxCounts`; add a completion-aware spawn option only if needed.
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` — expose/retain live minions long enough for the
  sweep to explode them (e.g. a read-before-destroy accessor).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — existing `destroySelf()` / `playExplosion(scale)`
  seams consumed by the sweep (no reward side effects).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — gym destroy seam used by the
  sweep in the gym.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§3.3, §4.4.4),
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — defeat-flow documentation.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — parity guards that must keep passing.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z (completed) — mini-boss epic; this sweep refines its
  defeat behaviour.
- AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5 (completed) — `PlayScene` mini-boss integration
  (`_damageMiniBoss` defeat path this change extends).
- AH-0MVCRAV3B0069AIJ (completed) — `WaveManager` per-level mini-boss gating
  (the wave-advance-once constraint).
- AH-0MVH85XXZ008INE2 (completed) — mini-boss left-behind graphics; precedent
  for tearing the encounter down cleanly on defeat.
- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH (completed) — mini-boss reward overlay
  (`openMiniBossReward`, `miniBossRewardOpen`), the overlay this change delays.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F (completed) — reward-overlay demo auto-select; must not
  stall behind the new delay.
- AH-0MVCB6LBE007I6R8 (open) — "Stop firing when boss is destroyed": related
  post-destruction cleanup pattern at the final boss; check for a shared
  "defeat moment" seam rather than duplicating gating logic.
- AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB (completed) — staggered
  multi-burst celebration scheduling (`spawnVictoryFireworks`) to mirror.
- AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY (open) — "Explosions sould be explosions": image-based
  explosion rendering; overlaps the VFX module but is orthogonal (visual
  quality vs defeat-sweep behaviour).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (completed) — the shared particle explosion module this
  change reuses.

Duplicate check: performed (keywords "explosions", "mini-boss", "reward
screen", "chain explosion") — **no overlapping completed item found**; the
nearest items (VFX quality AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY, final-boss victory fireworks
AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) do not cover a mini-boss-defeat
explosion sweep.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** applies to the **mini-boss defeat only**. Extending the
  sweep to the final boss or ordinary wave clears is separate work (record as
  discovered work items, not scope).
- **Particle budget:** up to 40 bursts in a short window. Mitigation: extra and
  anchored bursts use a modest enemy-scale size/scale and a reduced particle
  count; the sweep is bounded by `max(0, 30 − n) + 10 + n ≤ 40` bursts.
- **Double-advance risk:** `_damageMiniBoss` already has a stale-count
  reconciliation that can replay `onEnemyDestroyed`; sweeping enemies changes
  the alive count, so tests must assert the level advance fires exactly once,
  after the sweep.
- **Minion teardown ordering** (see Constraints) — capture before destroy, or
  minions vanish without exploding and `n` is under-counted.
- **Pause ordering:** the overlay's pause freezes tweens; completion must be
  driven by real tween completion (or an explicit timer derived from burst
  lifespan + stagger), not by a frame count that could be frozen.
- **Assumption:** the 10 mini-boss bursts are anchored at the death position
  captured at destruction (same discipline as the victory fireworks anchor), not
  at the entity's (already destroyed) live coordinates.
- **Assumption:** "scattered randomly across the scene" means uniformly sampled
  within the playfield inset by the burst radius, so no explosion is clipped
  entirely off-screen. If the producer expects the full screen edge-to-edge,
  only the inset constant changes.
- **Assumption:** the sweep is a visual-only celebration; the mini-boss reward
  remains the only reward for the encounter (operator Q2 = B + C).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Per entry: question, answer, answering party, evidence.

- **Q1 (scope of "all remaining enemies")** — "Which live entities count as
  'all remaining enemies' and explode on the sweep: (a) everything alive on the
  field — escort ships, mini-boss-summoned minions, and hazards (asteroids, lane
  traffic); (b) wave-gating enemies only (escorts + minions, exclude hazards);
  or (c) escort ships only (exclude minions and hazards)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "1. B"** — wave-gating enemies only: escort ships plus
  the mini-boss's live minions; hazards (asteroids, lane traffic) are excluded
  and survive. Recommended option was (b); operator selected (b). Source:
  interactive reply. Research: `PlayScene.spawned` holds one entry per live
  entity including hazards; `isNonBlockingHazard`
  (`src/scenes/core/waveTimeout.ts`) is the shared hazard classifier, and
  `MiniBoss.getMinions()` exposes the entity-owned minions.
- **Q2 (kill semantics)** — "Should sweep-destroyed enemies be real kills — (a)
  full shared kill path (score, mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops, telemetry)
  with wave-advance batched to sweep end; (b) cosmetic explosions only —
  enemies removed visually, no score/drops; or (c) destroyed without any reward
  or telemetry?"
  — **Answer (operator): "2. B + C"** — treat as (b) cosmetic explosions only
  **and** (c) no reward or telemetry: enemies are removed visually with their
  explosion VFX, and award no score, no mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops and no
  kill telemetry (wave bookkeeping still updates so the level completes). Source:
  interactive reply. Recommended option was (a); operator overrode it with
  B + C. Research: `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` is the reward-bearing path and
  must **not** be used by the sweep; `BaseEnemy.destroySelf()` marks the entity
  dead and plays its explosion only, so it is the correct seam.
- **Q3 (count formula edges)** — "With n remaining enemies, the spec says
  `30 − n` extra scattered explosions. When n ≥ 30 (or 0), what should happen:
  (a) clamp extra at 0 — total scattered bursts = `max(30, n)` from enemy bursts
  + extras, plus the fixed 10 at the mini-boss; (b) always fire at least 30
  scattered extras regardless of n; or (c) always fire exactly 30 scattered
  extras on top of the n enemy bursts (total `30 + n`)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "3. A"** — clamp the extra count at 0:
  `extras = max(0, 30 − n)`, so `n = 0` gives 30 extras and `n ≥ 30` gives none;
  the 10 mini-boss-anchored bursts are always additional. Source: interactive
  reply. Recommended option was (a); operator selected (a). Research: at a clean
  defeat `n` is usually small (escorts cleared first), but carry-over survivors
  and minions can push `n` higher, so the clamp keeps the display bounded
  (`total bursts ≤ n + max(0, 30 − n) + 10 ≤ 40`).
